extracted.intended_audience: architects, architectural designers, and students/enthusiasts of architectural ornamentation
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and aesthetic criteria for designing and applying ornament to roofs, ridges, finials, vaults, ceilings, dormers, and vestibules — balancing structure, regional conditions, and naturalistic inspiration. Includes practical cautions (durability, scale, function) and philosophical principles about art imitating/correcting nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archivolt ornament distinct from tracery
rubrics_metrics.description: I have kept the inquiry into the proper ornament of the archivolt wholly free from all confusion with the questions of beauty in tracery; for, in fact, all tracery is a mere multiplication and entanglement of small archivolts, and its cusp ornament is a minor condition of that proper to the spandril.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat archivolt ornament as a separate design problem from the disposition of tracery bars. Tracery develops from the innermost shafts/fillets bent into forms chosen by the designer and reaches its defined form only after jamb and archivolt are divided into longitudinal mouldings. Study dedicated works (e.g., Edmund Sharpe on Decorated Windows) for principles and chronological/mechanical structure before judging aesthetic merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect interior vs exterior expression
rubrics_metrics.description: One side of a wall is... the same as another, and if its structure be concealed, it is mostly on the inside; but, in the roof, the anatomical structure... is visible, if at all, in the interior only: so that the subject of internal ornament becomes both wide and important, and that of external, comparatively subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External ornaments may be allowed some variance from the building's intended temper because passers-by may not be in the proper mood; interiors must fit the temper of those who enter. Avoid incongruous or profane subjects in interiors (though medieval builders sometimes used grotesques sparingly). Interior decoration should be governed by the use and spiritual/psychological purpose of the space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let decoration spring from structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever the ribs and beams are simply and unaffectedly arranged, there is no difficulty about decoration; the beams may be carved, the ribs moulded... but when the vaulting is unribbed... or the ceiling is flat, it becomes a difficult question how far their surfaces may receive ornamentation independent of their structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design ornamentation to arise naturally from the roof's anatomical elements (ribs, beams, vaults). Avoid applying ornament that ignores structural logic; independent ornament on unribbed vaults/flat ceilings often appears meaningless or mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid flat ceilings when possible; use painting/panelling carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: I have never myself seen a flat ceiling satisfactorily decorated, except by painting... On the whole, flat ceilings are as much to be avoided as possible; and, when necessary, perhaps a panelled ornamentation with rich colored patterns is the most satisfying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a flat ceiling must be used, prefer painted panels (on stretched canvas) or rich colored panelling rather than meaningless carving. Be mindful of durability (author notes paintings on canvas risk being soaked by rain when improperly sited). A blank ceiling is not redeemed by an added decorative ventilator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve the sweep of curved surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The majesty of a roof is never... as when the eye can pass undisturbed over the course of all its curvatures, and trace the dying of the shadows along its smooth and sweeping vaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disturb or break the serenity of a curved surface with inappropriate ornament; where possible prefer plain ridged vaults with visible stone. Use mosaics or fresco that follow the curvature (they do not break it). Avoid decorations that disturb the curve without adding real interest (the 'vulgar panelling' of St. Peter's and the Pantheon cited as detestable examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: External roof treatment should follow climate and regional character
rubrics_metrics.description: The outside surface is of small importance in central Europe, being almost universally low in slope... but the later Eastern and Arabian domes become elaborate in ornamentation... to the mind of an inhabitant of the north, a roof is a guard against wild weather; not a surface which is forever to bask in serene heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match roof decoration to local climate and roof function: northern roofs are naturally simple and massed against weather; low-slope Italian roofs (round tile) act as decoration; terraces and eastern domes may warrant different treatments. Do not import decoration unsuitable to regional/functional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tile and shingle shaping to create distant ornament (scale effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: On steep domestic roofs, there is no ornament better than may be obtained by merely rounding, or cutting to an angle, the lower extremities of the flat tiles or shingles... thus the whole surface is covered with an appearance of scales, a fish-like defence against water, at once perfectly simple, natural, and effective at any distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple, structural surface treatments (shaped tiles, rounded/cut shingle edges) to create rich distant effects. This 'scale armor' motif also enriches spires and pinnacles and is often superior to applied surface ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dormer windows must be legitimate and serviceable
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether dormer windows are legitimately to be classed as decorative features, seems to me to admit of doubt... such windows are never to be allowed in places visibly inaccessible, or on less than a natural and serviceable scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dormers derive from domestic lookout windows and should be functional and credibly sited. Avoid purely decorative or inaccessible dormers and those that are out of scale with serviceability — do not fake functionality for ornament's sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat fringes, finials, and crockets as parasitical features requiring caution
rubrics_metrics.description: As there is no use in any of these things, and as they are visible additions and parasitical portions of the structure, more caution is required in their use than in any other features of ornament...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because ridge/point decorations are unapplied, visible appendages, they must be used sparingly and subordinately. They work best where a playful northern spirit is fitting, but can undermine majesty if dominant. The architect and spectator must both be 'in felicitous humor' for them to succeed. Poorly conceived spikes/fringes look contrived or mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use finials and crockets as highlights — few, delicate, well-spaced
rubrics_metrics.description: Stone finials and crockets are, I think, to be considered in architecture, what points and flashes of light are in the color of painting... better to avoid breaking up either lines or masses by too many points, and to make the few points used exceedingly precious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place finials/crockets like stars along lines at considerable intervals, executed with exquisite delicacy and fancy. Small ones may be more frequent and can describe lines by a chain of points, but clustering or bunching destroys their value. Over-indulgence marks lowness of school. Note: Venice's best architecture often lacks crockets/finials; exemplary uses appear in Giotto's tower and Pisan works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornament should imitate and 'correct' nature according to nature's rules
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the highest aim of every art to imitate nature, this is not to be done by imitating any natural form, but by criticising and correcting it, — criticising it by Nature's rules gathered from all her works... 'the artist's object was to make things not as Nature makes them, but as she would make them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use natural forms as the source of ornament but apply judgment and correction to render them more 'conformable to the general tendency of Nature.' The artist's role is explanatory rather than arrogant improvement — gather and present the readable, representative part of nature rather than attempting impossible perfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture's moral/aesthetic function: evoke and replace fellowship with nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of our architecture is, as far as may be, to replace these; to tell us about nature; to possess us with memories of her quietness; to be solemn and full of tenderness, like her, and rich in portraitures of her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge architecture by whether it gives a delight and instruction akin to that of nature. If built work can furnish pure and intense delight like a valley among hills, it is right; if it gives no such instruction or joy, condemn it. Architecture should remedy urban loss of natural fellowship by embodying nature's qualities rather than mere affectation or ornament without feeling.
